rationale: Start with a broad, mid-strength scouting gradient at moderate temperature to reveal the overall elution window and whether all 10 compounds elute within 42 min. This should give useful spacing information without a high risk of truncation.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing analysis time. Keep composition and temperature fixed and shorten the gradient one step to see if t_last drops while maintaining all pair resolutions above 1.5.

We are very close to the 10 min threshold and still have margin on the worst pair, so shorten the gradient another step. This tests whether we can eliminate the remaining time penalty while keeping the critical pair resolved.

At 14 min the only loss is the critical pair just below full-credit resolution, so keep the faster gradient and lower temperature one step to increase retention/selectivity slightly. This may recover R(6,7) to at least 1.5 while keeping t_last near or under 10 min.

Lowering temperature hurt selectivity badly, so probe the opposite direction at the fast 14 min gradient. A 5 C increase may improve the critical mid-eluting pair enough to reach full resolution credit while keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min.

Temperature changes worsened the critical region, so keep the successful 40 C and instead slightly narrow the gradient window by lowering phi1 one step. This should strengthen retention late in the run and may spread the crowded mid-eluting cluster enough to push the worst pair above 1.5 while likely keeping t_last near 10 min.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so now map the robustness boundary by making the method one step faster while keeping the successful gradient window and temperature. If full resolution holds, this gives a shorter equivalent optimum; if not, injection 6 remains the best method.

Since shortening tG lost resolution at the same critical pair, keep tG at the optimal 14 min and test a slightly lower phi1 to see whether the full-resolution optimum can be made more robust or shifted to a stronger-separation setting. This explores whether additional late-gradient retention improves the crowded mid-run region without pushing t_last too far past 10 min.

The optimum appears very localized around phi1 = 0.85, so test a slightly higher starting strength while keeping the winning endpoint and slope region. Raising phi0 may pull the last peak just under 10 min while preserving enough selectivity in the critical mid-eluting pair.

Injection 9 improved the fully resolved method by pulling t_last comfortably below 10 min while keeping some margin on the critical pair, so now try the next faster gradient at the same composition. This tests whether the stronger start allows a shorter run without dropping the worst-pair resolution below 1.5.

The 12 min gradient still loses resolution at the same critical pair, so keep tG at 14 min and test a slightly stronger start to see if t_last can be reduced further while maintaining full-credit separation. This refines around the current optimum and may identify a shorter practical maximum-CRF method.

The best region is clearly centered at phi0 = 0.10–0.15 and phi1 = 0.85, and increasing phi0 further hurt the critical pair. Test a slightly wider, steeper window from the current best start to see whether phi1 = 0.90 improves the critical selectivity enough to keep full resolution while retaining the sub-10 min last peak.

The best methods lie on a narrow boundary where the critical pair is just resolved, so test the opposite direction in phi0 from injection 9. Lowering phi0 may slightly increase selectivity for the crowded pair while keeping the successful phi1 = 0.85 endpoint, and will show whether injection 9 is the center or edge of the optimum plateau.

The two best methods are at phi1 = 0.85, and changing phi0 shows a tradeoff between t_last and the critical pair margin. Test phi0 = 0.15 with a slightly lower phi1 to see whether this combination preserves full resolution while still keeping the last peak near 10 min, helping define the local optimum more completely.

We already have maximum-CRF methods at 40 C, so use remaining budget to probe robustness of the best composition against temperature at the winning tG. Testing 45 C at phi0 = 0.10, phi1 = 0.85 shows whether the optimum is narrowly temperature-dependent or whether a warmer, potentially faster-equilibrating variant still holds full resolution.

The best score is already achieved, so use the remaining budget to map whether temperature effects are monotonic around the winning composition. A higher temperature than 45 C will confirm whether the collapse of the critical pair continues, strengthening confidence that 40 C is the true optimum operating point.

We have confirmed that increasing temperature strongly collapses the critical pair, so test the lower-temperature side at the other maximum-CRF composition. This checks robustness of the best practical method and whether phi0 = 0.15 is more or less temperature-sensitive than phi0 = 0.10.

With the optimum already found, use one injection to define the slower-side robustness of the winning composition. A 16 min version at the same phi values will show how much resolution margin is gained for only a modest time penalty and helps confirm the local tradeoff surface around the optimum.

A lower phi1 improved the critical pair margin but cost some late retention time at 14 min, so test whether shortening that more retentive window balances the tradeoff. This is a plausible alternative route to a full-resolution method faster than 14 min if the critical pair stays above 1.5.

The phi0 = 0.15, phi1 = 0.80 setting gave the best critical-pair margin among nearby variants but was just over the 10 min threshold at 14 min, so test the neighboring slower slope only to complete the tradeoff picture. This should confirm that extra resolution comes at too much time cost relative to the existing 1.000 methods.

With the optimum already secured, use the remaining injections to finish mapping the neighboring composition corners around the best region. This low-phi0/high-phi1 combination complements the tested 0.05/0.85 and 0.15/0.90 cases and helps confirm that the maximum sits specifically near phi0 = 0.10–0.15 and phi1 = 0.85.

Complete the local 2D composition map around the optimum by testing the stronger-start/lower-endpoint corner. This should confirm whether the loss seen at phi0 = 0.20 is mainly driven by phi0 itself or whether reducing phi1 can restore the critical-pair resolution.

This newly found maximum-CRF composition is a strong candidate for a faster optimum because it already keeps t_last well below 10 min at 14 min with full resolution. Test the 12 min version to see whether this composition, unlike the earlier maxima, can retain the critical pair above 1.5 and give a shorter equally optimal method.

The 0.20/0.80 composition gives maximum CRF with some margin on the critical pair, so take one final step stronger at the start to see if this edge of the optimum plateau can still hold full resolution while keeping t_last under 10 min. This is the most promising unexplored neighbor for finding the shortest practical maximum-CRF setting at the same 14 min gradient.

The final open question near the newly discovered optimum is whether a slightly lower phi1 can preserve full resolution at phi0 = 0.20 while staying under 10 min. This directly probes the remaining adjacent neighbor of the 0.20/0.80 maximum without repeating any prior method.
